questions.q: Which category prices trades by formula instead of an order book?
options: Stablecoins
DEXs / AMMs
Derivatives & perpetuals
Yield aggregators
questions.explain: AMMs like Uniswap and Curve use a pricing formula applied to pool reserves instead of matching buy and sell orders.

questions.q: What is the key structural difference between USDC and DAI as stablecoins?
options: USDC and DAI use the exact same collateral model
DAI is backed by fiat reserves and USDC is backed by crypto
USDC is fiat-collateralized by real-world dollar reserves; DAI is crypto-collateralized by an overcollateralized basket of on-chain assets
Neither stablecoin uses any form of collateral
questions.explain: USDC's value is backed by real dollars held in reserve off-chain; DAI's value comes from crypto collateral locked on-chain, held above the debt it backs.

questions.q: In the "one dollar's journey" example, what happens right after swapping USDC for ETH on an AMM?
options: The ETH is withdrawn to a bank account
The ETH is immediately burned
The ETH is swapped back into USDC
The ETH is deposited as collateral into a lending protocol
questions.explain: The sequence is: swap for ETH, supply that ETH as collateral in a lending protocol, then borrow a stablecoin against it.

questions.q: What does a yield aggregator like Yearn actually do?
options: It automates moving capital between other protocols (like lending pools and AMMs) to chase yield
It issues its own fiat-backed stablecoin
It runs a centralized order book for derivatives
It replaces the need for any collateral in lending
questions.explain: Yield aggregators don't invent a new primitive — they automate deposits into existing protocols like lending pools and AMM pools.

questions.q: Why does this course spend two full chapters specifically on AMMs and lending, rather than derivatives or stablecoins?
options: Because derivatives and stablecoins don't exist in DeFi
Because AMMs and lending solve the two load-bearing problems (trading without an order book, lending without a credit check) that other categories are built on top of
Because AMMs and lending are the newest categories to exist
Because this course considers derivatives and stablecoins unimportant
questions.explain: Derivatives, stablecoins, and yield products are all built from AMM and lending primitives underneath, which is why those two get the deepest treatment.
